title: Reserved pool coverage scenarios and negotiation cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick, negotiation-ready spreadsheet and one-pager that converts reserved GPU pool commits into play-ready pricing/coverage scenarios. Designed for product + sales handoff when customers want committed GPU pools but ask for blended rates or unusual coverage windows.

High-level assumptions (configurable cells):
- GPU types: A100-80GB, H100-80GB, A10G (spot mix option)
- Hourly raw cost (cloud): A100=3.20, H100=6.40, A10G=0.90 (USD/hr)
- Effective overhead (infra, egress, ops): 10%
- Expected average sustained utilization (configurable): 60% / 75% / 90% scenarios
- Commitment horizon: 12 / 24 / 36 months
- Discount target: customer asks for 30% off list CPU/GPU rate -> translate to per-token economics

Worksheet: Scenario sweep (rows are scenarios, columns are calc outputs)

Scenario ID | Commit (GPUs) | GPU type | Months | Cloud cost/hr | Overhead % | Util% | Effective billable hrs/mo | Total committed hrs | Amortized monthly raw | Monthly ops overhead | Total monthly cost | Cost per effective GPU-hr | Suggested list hourly price | Margin buffer | Target blended price | Break-even months at target price
S1-compact | 16 | A100 | 12 | 3.20 | 10% | 60% | 438 | 210,240 | $21,307 | $2,131 | $23,438 | $11.17 | 25% | $14.00 | 9
S2-growth | 64 | A100 | 24 | 3.20 | 10% | 75% | 546 | 1,055,808 | $107,181 | $10,718 | $117,899 | $8.90 | 30% | $11.60 | 11
S3-enterprise | 256 | H100 | 36 | 6.40 | 10% | 90% | 657 | 6,044,352 | $1,221,568 | $122,157 | $1,343,725 | $9.83 | 20% | $11.80 | 18
S4-preemptable-mix | 128 | mix(A100+A10G) | 12 | weighted=2.20 | 12% | 65% | 474 | 729,024 | $342,658 | $41,119 | $383,777 | $7.44 | 35% | $10.00 | 7

Notes on columns and formulas (human-readable):
- Effective billable hrs/mo = 24 * 30 * Util% * number_of_GPUs
- Total committed hrs = months * 24 * 30 * GPUs
- Amortized monthly raw = cloud_cost/hr * committed_GPUs * 24 * 30 / months (amortized evenly across months)
- Ops overhead = Amortized monthly raw * overhead %
- Cost per effective GPU-hr = Total monthly cost / Effective billable hrs/mo
- Suggested list hourly price = cost per effective GPU-hr * (1 + margin buffer) / (1 - expected discounts)  (approx; sales uses blended adjustments)
- Break-even months = Fixed provisioning and one-time migration credits / monthly gross margin (for multi-year migration incentives)

Guidance: converting to per-token economics
- Baseline tokens/hour for typical decoder model = 50k tokens/hr at avg seq length 64 (customer-specific)
- Derive token cost: token_cost = (Cost per effective GPU-hr) / tokens_per_hour
- Round to per-1k-token units for quoting (easier for product sales)

Negotiation cheats (playbook snippets):
1) Anchor on utilization, not nominal GPU count. "We price based on sustainable utilization that keeps your SLOs intact" — propose a utilization ramp schedule (month 1-3 at 40%, months 4-6 at 60%, steady state 75%).
2) Offer an "Ops credit" convertible to free 1-month burst capacity if customer commits 24+ months (shifts some up-front cost into measurable ops value).
3) Provide a preemptable mix bucket to shave 12-25% from blended list for batch workloads, but cap SLA to non-critical jobs only.
4) Use a layered discount: commit size -> duration -> regional placement -> prepay cadence. Present as discrete buckets to keep calculus simple.
5) Push tradeoffs: higher utilization guarantees = lower blended price. Have a one-page chart to show marginal $/GPU-hr if utilization increases by 5–10%.

Sample sales note (one-liner to send to customer during negotiation):
"We modeled three coverage options for your traffic mix: a compact starter pool (lower entry, faster breakeven), a scaled growth pool (best unit economics at 24mo), and a mixed preemptable pool for batch cost-savings. Which one should I open a fixed quote for so we can lock the regional capacity?"

Common rebuttals and suggested responses:
- "We need a lower list price": Show utilization curve and offer a phased utilization SLA with a higher initial price, automatic step-down as utilization increases.
- "We want a blended rate across models": Offer model family buckets with small delta per family and a clear fallback to on-demand for new model experimentation.
- "We want credits for migration": Convert credits into a time-limited ops credit or temporary extra GPU hours so fixed monthly cost remains simple.

Action items and next steps (owner tags):
- Priya: finalize weighted GPU-cost model for H100+A100 mix (due 2024-11-15)
- Diego: run historical workload simulator to produce utilization ramp scenarios from three reference customers (JIRA DED-5123) (due 2024-11-22)
- Maya: draft sales one-pager with charts and marginal delta table (due 2024-11-19)
- Owen: implement scenario sheet as a templated Google Sheet and add to sales template library (PR: repo/redwood-dedicated/pr/341) (due 2024-11-25)

Open questions (to resolve before next review):
- Should we include network egress-tiering into the amortization assumptions for multi-region customers? (impact: +2–8%)
- Standardize "tokens/hr" benchmark per customer workload class or let SEs supply per-account numbers?

Back-of-envelope quick rules (for on-call pricing conversations):
- Rule A: Each +10% utilization on a committed pool reduces unit cost by ~7–9% (depends on GPU mix).
- Rule B: Moving 25% of batch to preemptable capacity yields ~12–18% blended discount, but cap at 35% of total pool to avoid disruption.
- Rule C: 24-month commitments typically hit an amortization sweet spot for 40–120 GPU pools; beyond ~200 GPUs, push 36 months for deeper amortization.

Reference snippets to paste into quote templates:
- "Blended commit price assumes a 75% sustainable utilization and includes a 10% infra/ops overlay. Preemptable mix options available for batch workloads."
- "Commit discounts are applied on top of list hourly rates; final blended price scales with realized utilization and can be reconciled quarterly."
summary: Scenario-driven spreadsheet and negotiation guide for translating reserved GPU commits into actionable quotes and playbook for sales. Includes scenario table, formulas, playbook snippets, action items, and open questions.
